decisions.question: What surface carries the durable fold record, across the three deletion sites?
decisions.outcome: A single shared append-only index at docs/folds.md, created on first append, one row per completed fold, written mechanically by /scope Phase 2 at every hop that folds. Site 3 (/execute's cascade deletion of the PLAN) is declared out of R20 with its reason recorded. R21's frontmatter declaration and ## Status line are untouched -- different requirement, different beneficiary.
decisions.row_contents: date, absorbed artifact's repo-relative path, survivor (or 'none' at the terminal fold), verdict, a mechanical serialization of the state file's existing carry_check mapping (section names and outcomes, never section text), and the git hash-object blob SHA of the pre-fold original.
decisions.hash_provenance: Recomputed at fold time, NOT promoted from child_snapshots.content_hash -- that value is captured post-invocation and the drift machinery exists precisely because it can differ from the live bytes, while R20 requires the hash of what was actually deleted.
six_mechanics: The record is on disk and staged before anything is deleted, so R30's fail-toward-keep is structural rather than procedural.

git add docs/folds.md beside the existing git rm. /scope never commits -- the absorb is a bare git rm and the upstream re-point is an unstaged working-tree edit -- and git commit -a does not stage an untracked file. Without this the deletion lands and the record does not. Four of five validators reached this independently.

docs/folds.md joins R15's exclusion clause beside wip/ and the survivor. Without it the record refuses the NEXT hop's fold, because the row names a still-live survivor by path. Re-pointing prior rows was rejected as barred by 'R15 aborts before any mutation'; bare-naming was rejected as trading the record's most useful field for a dismissable finding on every cascading fold.
On an R18 revert the row is removed, not marked. R20's criterion is scoped to a completed fold, and the row is uncommitted at that point, so removal is a line edit.

The checker is deletion-driven (git diff --diff-filter=D) and lives in validate-docs.yml -- the REUSABLE workflow adopters pin, because folds happen in adopter repos and a shirabe-local check would leave every adopter's destructive operation unverified. It already sets fetch-depth: 0, so git rev-parse BASE:<path> recovers the pre-fold blob; check-sentinel.yml and pr-body.yml are depth 1 and cannot.
One line of .gitattributes: docs/folds.md merge=union. Verified by running it -- without a driver two branches appending produce a conflict; with it, a clean merge keeping both rows.
decisions.why_the_r20_ruling_decided_it: Under 'the default branch keeps a record', every surface living inside a chain document is disqualified: this repository merges a whole chain as one squash, so any document a later hop folds away takes its record with it. That kills the hybrid in the case the feature exists to serve -- a self-contained fix that folds down to its code -- and kills the minimal answer outright, since the terminal fold is exactly where the corpus otherwise retains no evidence the work happened.
decisions.write_target_amendment: Explicit, not a quiet widening: one bullet in phase-3-exit-finalization.md and one in SKILL.md; corrects 'one deletion target' to one deletion and one append target; corrects 'Phase 3 does not delete; it records' to name Phase 2 as the recorder; adds a Phase 4 carve-out so the file is enumerated but never swept; rewrites the absorb steps in phase-2. The path is a fixed constant with nothing interpolated, which is stronger for the injection argument than the slug-composed paths already in the set.
decisions.pre_existing_defects_folded_in: The current set gates docs/{briefs,prds,designs}/ writes on force-materialization only, so the full-run absorb's mutation of the survivor is ALREADY outside the enumerated set; and SKILL.md names docs/plans/ while phase-3 says Phase 3 does not write it. R19 owes both fixes regardless of this decision.
decisions.execute_impact: None. /execute needs no change at all for this decision.

decisions.question: Who authors a contribution section: the child at drafting time, or the parent at fold time?
decisions.outcome: Parent composes the contribution section at fold time, sourced from the SURVIVOR's own body -- not from the doomed original -- with the child owning the consumption instruction that puts the material into the survivor in the first place.
decisions.why_child_authoring_is_eliminated: Not outscored, ruled out by settled requirements: the judgment is step 8 of Phase 2's eight-step loop, so a child cannot know the verdict at draft time, and every keep run would leave an orphan section R4 does not sanction and R10's carve-out (scoped to the absorbed case) does not cover. formats.rs has no per-section optionality primitive to express a conditional one.
decisions.why_sourcing_from_the_survivor_matters: It makes the non-independence tolerable: the material was already jury-reviewed when it landed in the survivor's ordinary sections, and an under-distillation leaves the omitted content still visible in the survivor's body rather than gone at git rm.
decisions.file_count_for_plan: ~9 instruction files. Child consumption instructions: skills/prd/references/phases/phase-3-draft.md (AMEND), skills/design/references/phases/phase-2-execution.md (NEW), skills/plan/references/phases/phase-7-creation.md (NEW). /brief needs none. Plus 4 format references and 2 /scope phase files. Zero jury prompt files.
corrections_to_prior_decisions: D1's stated rationale is falsified in one clause. It rejected a fold-time reviewer because 'the child's own jury reads the upstream and the draft together, with a spawn already budgeted.' The tactical juries do NOT receive the upstream -- verified across /prd, /design and /brief reviewer prompts. D1's conclusion survives; its reason must be replaced with R12's structural bar.

The structural bar is stronger than recorded. parent-skill-pattern.md binds dispatch to the Skill tool called inline from the parent's own agent context, so parent and child SHARE one agent context. The child/parent fork was never about which agent holds the pen -- only about which instruction file holds the drafting instruction, and therefore whether the child's jury spawns see the section.
decisions.pre_existing_defect_found: /scope's closed write-target set already understates the parent's reach: the existing upstream: re-point writes the survivor and is not listed. R19 fixes this regardless of which answer won.

decisions.question: Do the two contradicted claims in the shipped consolidation chain get amended, and how?
decisions.outcome: amend both via appended dated Amendment sections; original prose untouched, no lifecycle change
decisions.precedent: commit 26465a2 (PR #224) amended a Done PRD, a Current DESIGN and a BRIEF together, append-only
decisions.scope_widened: Decision 8 of the shipped DESIGN is also falsified, and more severely than Decision 9: its chosen Option A concluded the smallest reachable set is PRD+DESIGN+PLAN and that a zero-artifact run is unreachable, both of which R11 falsifies — and its rejected Option D (make DESIGN absorbable into PLAN) is exactly what R11 adopts. Decision 9's conclusion survives on other grounds; Decision 8's does not.

decisions.question: What replaces the type-level first stage: does it dissolve into the content judgment, or become a different check?
decisions.outcome: The type test and the mapping table are deleted. The position survives as a Citation Preflight whose sole content is R15's citation search relocated to run before the content question -- mechanical, body-blind, type-blind, able to return only 'proceed' or 'keep'. R2's scoping moves OUT of the stage to the firing condition at step 8, reading chain_ran: membership.
decisions.why_not_full_dissolution: Dissolution was the serious rival and lost on one point: it does not remove the attractor that already filled this position once with a hand-authored type table, it relocates that attractor to the head of the content stage -- which is the stage that CAN return absorb and where no ceiling applies. A type-shaped shortcut is worse there, not better.
decisions.structural_clauses: (1) A stated ceiling: the stage cannot reach any outcome stronger than keep, in R15's own shipped words. (2) An input restriction: no check in the judgment may read either type's required-section list or compare the two types' section sets. Chain position and provenance are admissible; a type's content contract is not. Test for a violation: a condition that refuses one pair while permitting its structural twin under identical repository state is a type rule. Written at the head of the content stage too, because that is where absorb is reachable.
verified_facts_that_reshaped_it: The mapping table's claim to be 'derived from the per-type required-section contracts in formats.rs, not enumerated by hand' is FALSE. formats.rs holds only per-format required_sections lists; there is no mapping structure anywhere in crates/. Every semantic edge in the table is authored prose, and the table silently drops Status from the BRIEF's five required sections. Its re-derivation instruction has never been runnable.

Non-adjacent hops are reachable today and undefined. Re-entry protection plus four children yields brief->design, prd->plan and brief->plan; brief->design is produced by shipped eval id 8, and the table has no row for it. An absent row is neither total nor not-total, so the procedure has no defined next action.

R15 cannot cover those hops. The deletion target at a non-adjacent hop is always minutes old, and a document written before the run cannot cite one created during it -- disjoint by construction. All 36 BRIEFs sit at a settled status, so every pre-existing BRIEF is held back by re-entry protection and can never be a run-produced upstream. Disjointness is total, not partial.
decisions.contradiction_the_design_must_settle: Phase 2's child-invocation table hard-codes '/design | docs/prds/PRD-<topic>.md' while the prose two lines above says the argument is 'the path of the nearest artifact this chain produced above it'. These disagree on exactly the eval-8 trace. Everything about non-adjacent hops is downstream of that one sentence.
decisions.absorbable_field: Retired, not re-annotated -- under R1 it would be true at every hop it could ever be written. Replaced by stage: preflight | judgment | carry, naming the stage at which the entry's verdict was settled. Free to change: the procedure has never executed, so there are no entries on disk to migrate. hop: and verdict: should also join Phase 2's enum re-validation list, which today covers four fields and omits verdict: despite the schema declaring it an enum.
decisions.floor_section: Replaced rather than edited, and moved from phase-1-discovery.md to Phase 2 beside the judgment. The /plan redirect goes with the premise -- an author wanting no durable record no longer has to leave /scope. The no-guard instruction survives with a corrected reason, sited in Phase 2 because that is where the unguarded temptation lives. The prohibition also becomes a graded expectation on rewritten eval id 18.
decisions.sharpest_finding: R27 does NOT forbid a floor guard -- a mechanism whose only possible effect is to force keep does not count as a second reduction mechanism. So the guard now looks reasonable to anyone not told why it is forbidden, which is why deleting the Floor section outright was rejected: the instruction is needed more than it was, not less.
decisions.chain_ran_write_site: Confirmed with a fourth consumer I had not found: Phase 3 reads chain_ran: in four places, including the R8 tie-break's per-child start timestamps. This work must create the write site, in Phase 2's loop step 6 alongside the child snapshot, with entries carrying a started-at timestamp so phase-3's existing claim about reading timestamps out of chain_ran: becomes true.
decisions.prd_amendment_applied: R30 amended from five decision points to four; its criterion retagged [mech] and bound to the preflight's single mechanical operation.

decisions.question: How does the validator represent and enforce contribution sections: the frontmatter declaration's shape and the required-sections extension?
decisions.declaration: New optional frontmatter key `absorbed:`, holding a scalar or sequence of repo-relative paths -- the same shape `upstream:` accepts, read through the same upstream::field_entries normalizer, inheriting trim/blank-drop/placeholder-skip for free. The absorbed TYPE is derived from the basename prefix via detect_format's longest-prefix rule; nothing declares the type redundantly.
decisions.why_paths_not_types: The PRD's own criterion requires the declaration to hold the absorbed path, and R21's named beneficiary is a reader holding a dead path who does not know the survivor exists. Type names alone strand exactly that reader and cannot distinguish this chain's PRD from another's.
decisions.why_flat: The frontmatter parser cannot read structure: a mapping value becomes FieldEntries::Other and its nested pairs are discarded unrecoverably; a sequence of mappings becomes Sequence with empty item text. So the declaration is a flat list of strings or it is a change to frontmatter.rs, which sits upstream of every check and both parity harnesses. Flat also keeps transitive accumulation linear: survivor.absorbed = ancestor.absorbed ++ [ancestor.path].
decisions.mechanism: required_sections_for (checks.rs:181) gains a second branch beside the execution_mode one, splicing the implied contribution headings immediately after the Status entry. Every one of the eight formats' required_sections lists begins with Status, as do all three Plan execution_mode lists, so the splice point is well-defined with no per-format special case. Returns the base list unchanged when `absorbed:` is absent -- which is every document on disk today.
decisions.new_check: One error-level code FC17, gated entirely on `absorbed:` being present. Four clauses: (1) the field yields at least one usable entry -- malformed shapes are an error, not a silent no-op, which is the fail-closed call; (2) every entry's basename matches a prefix in the contribution table and is not cross-repo; (3) every entry's type sits strictly above the carrying document's own type in the chain; (4) the implied sections appear contiguously and immediately after ## Status, in chain order.
decisions.why_fc17_is_not_a_severity_workaround: check_fc15 compares only the RELATIVE order of required sections present and explicitly permits unrequired sections between them, so a contribution section three headings below ## Status satisfies it at any severity. R4's placement is strictly stronger than FC15 can express. FC15 is also registered notice-level behind a documented promotion seam that waits on a corpus-cleanup PR, and promoting it is exactly the R29 breakage that seam exists to avoid.
decisions.headings: const CONTRIBUTION_SECTIONS: [(&str,&str);4] in formats.rs, keyed by prefix: BRIEF- -> 'Absorbed Brief', PRD- -> 'Absorbed PRD', DESIGN- -> 'Absorbed Design', PLAN- -> 'Absorbed Plan'. Array position gives both R6's chain order and FC17 clause 3's strict comparison. Needs no new FormatSpec field and no edit to the eight existing constructors.
decisions.collision_check: Checked against the union of every required section of all eight formats plus the three Plan execution-mode lists (46 distinct names): no name begins with 'Absorbed'. Grep over docs/, crates/ and skills/ finds no ^## Absorbed heading and no absorbed: key anywhere today.
decisions.r21_satisfied_by_construction: Only upstream: is ever resolved as a path (by R6, L04 and the finalization walk). superseded_by:, the nearest analogue, is never resolved at all. So R21's path-resolution exclusion is satisfied by construction; the obligation is the negative one of not adding absorbed: to those three readers.

decisions.question: How is the pre-deletion citation guard implemented, and does it live in skill prose or in the validator?
decisions.outcome: tested shell script skills/scope/scripts/check-citations.sh doing the search (git grep -I -F -n per tier, pinned pathspec exclusions); verdict routing stays in Stage 3 prose; co-located _test.sh under a new check-scope-scripts.yml merge gate
decisions.timing_correction: runs at the TOP of Stage 3, before the contribution is authored and before the upstream re-point -- so a downgrade is a pure abort with nothing to undo. Supersedes the exploration's 'between the re-point and the git rm' placement.
decisions.load_bearing_measurement: the survivor always cites the absorbed artifact via its own upstream:, so a naive search blocks 36 of 36 BRIEF/PRD folds. Excluding the survivor as a file brings it to 20/36; excluding only the upstream: line is insufficient because 22 of 36 survivors cite the path more than once. The exclusion set is the difference between a guard and a total fold-blocker, which is why it needs a test rather than prose.
decisions.coverage_correction: build_referrer_map sees 77 of 271 path-citing lines (28%) because build_inverse_upstream only iterates indexed.upstreams -- blind to the 194 prose/References/code/CI citations including all three non-markdown ones.
consequences_for_design: The guard bites hard: 15 of 36 BRIEF/PRD pairs (42%) on today's corpus carry a genuine third-party path citation and would fold to keep.

/scope can permanently block itself: its own Decision Record templates write durable files under docs/decisions/ citing artifact paths verbatim, and that directory is tracked, outside wip/, and not a fixture. Correct under R30 but a designed outcome that belongs in prose.

The survivor's own now-dead prose citations (22 of 36 pairs) are a rewrite obligation on the fold, not a block -- excluding the survivor is what makes folding possible, so something else must clean them.
